title.narrative: Community-led Climate Resilient and Sustainable Livelihood Program in Coastal Areas of Satkhira District.

description.narrative: 5,000 households from marginalised communities in Debhata Upazila, Satkhira Sadar Upazila and the urban slums in Satkhira Municipality are less vulnerable to the negative effects of climate change in terms of health and finances.Objective 1:5,000 households from marginalized communities have access to improved and safe basic sanitationObjective 2:500 households benefit from divesified and increased agricultural production all year round.Objective 3:200 women at risk can draw on strengthened entrepreneurial skills.

Satkhira Municipality: The direct beneficiaries are 6,250 people (60% women) from 1,250 households with an average of 5 household members (including 77 households from Dalits/minorities and 1-2% people with disabilities). These climate migrants are technically IDPs with no specific legal status, but have problems obtaining official registrations and/or (ID) papers.Rural areas in Satkhira Sadar Upazila (Fingri Union) and Debhata Upazila (Kulia and Parulia Union): The direct beneficiaries are 18,750 people (53% women) who comprise 3,750 households (5% Dalit/minority households and 3% people with disabilities). The project, Community-Based Programme for Climate-Resilient and Sustainable Livelihoods in Satkhira, Bangladesh, aims to empower 5,000 marginalized households (25,000 people) against climate change impacts. Running from 15 November 2024 to 15 November 2027, it addresses vulnerabilities in water, sanitation, livelihoods, and governance. Key interventions include installing solar-powered water systems, climate-resilient sanitation, and promoting solid waste management. The project enhances sustainable agriculture, income diversification, and women-led green enterprises, including biodegradable sanitary napkins. It strengthens local governance for climate adaptation and builds organizational capacities of partners to ensure long-term impact.
